business_problem: Chongqing's courts needed to reduce the repetitive workload of clerks and judges, especially in transcription, evidence review, case lookup, and document drafting, while improving the speed and consistency of judicial handling.
solution_summary: Chongqing High People's Court and Baidu AI Cloud built the Easy Trial platform using OCR, NLP, and real-time speech recognition to support multiple judicial workflows. Uploaded litigation materials are classified automatically and key fields are filled back into case records. During hearings, speech recognition converts courtroom audio into text so clerks are not tied to manual transcription and appellate judges can locate important remarks quickly in long recordings. The same AI layer also powers similar-case recommendation and intelligent document generation, giving judges precedent-style references, legal knowledge graphs, and drafting support throughout the case lifecycle. The platform sits inside the court's broader '4+1' smart-court ecosystem, where Easy Trial is one of four major platforms and the 'Law Intelligence Cloud Center' provides shared intelligence support.

data_flow: Litigation documents and hearing audio enter the Easy Trial platform, where OCR and speech recognition convert them into structured text. NLP services then route the information into case files, similar-case recommendations, legal knowledge views, and document-generation workflows that support judges and clerks.
business_outcome: Chongqing courts reduced clerical repetition, accelerated similar-case research and document drafting, and gave judicial staff a more efficient digital-assistance layer for case handling.
